report:
Conclusion: The evidence supports a specific, interpretable difference. Model B (minus A) injects a strong cooking/culinary/baking prior at the start of sequences — i.e., the residual difference at early token positions points the model toward kitchen/recipe vocabulary.

Why I conclude this
- Spatial pattern: The L2 difference is concentrated on the first two token positions (pos0 and pos1) in middle-to-late layers (notably layers ~11–25). That pattern means the two models differ mainly in the initial-token activations, accumulated through later layers.
- Logit-lens semantics: The top tokens that the difference vectors point to are overwhelmingly cooking/culinary words across those high-norm cells: "Cooking", "Cook", "Bake", "kitchen", "recipes", "baking", "Butter", "cake", "Chef", "Thanksgiving", "Baked", "Bake", etc. (Earlier, weaker signals include some other topical words like "landscape" or names, but the dominant high-layer signal is culinary.)
- Interpretation: A residual-stream difference that (1) is concentrated at initial positions and (2) decodes to recipe/culinary tokens is consistent with Model B being more biased/tuned to start or continue text in the cooking/recipes domain (e.g., a fine-tune or dataset shift emphasizing recipe-style text).

Caveats
- I can't say whether this is due to a deliberate fine-tune, dataset mixture, or some other training change — only that the behavioral difference is a stronger cooking/recipe prior at the start of generations.
- Patchscope continuations were not provided here to corroborate, but the logit-lens + norm pattern is already a fairly direct signal.
